messages.subject: Shiny URL processing
parts:
When you run the following code, you can click back and forth between the first two links and see the "search string" (the part of the URL after ?) change both in your browser's URL bar and on the page (after "search"). The search string part of the URL is in the session object, as documented here: https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/client-data.html.

However, when you click the third link, you'll get a 404 or Not Found error. I expected instead to be able to see "page2" in the session's pathname. It's been awhile since I've used php, but that how's I remember php code working.

The code below demonstrates that you could build a multi-page Shiny site if you're willing to use search strings, but why not with standard URLs?

Based on my distant experience with php I suspect the right server settings might fix this.  Does anyone know for sure?

library(shiny)


ui <- uiOutput("pageStub")


server <- function(input, output, session) {
   output$pageStub <- renderUI(
      fluidPage(fluidRow(
         column(12,
            HTML('<p>This is a link to <a href="?page2">?page2</a>',
                 '<p>This is a link back to the <a href=".">start folder</a>',
                 '<p>This is a link to <a href="page2">page2</a>',
                 "<p>pathname: ", session$clientData$url_pathname,
                 "<p>search: ",   session$clientData$url_search)
         )
      ))
   )
}


# Run the application
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.author: 4317e7b9c140bf2d
messages.subject: Re: Shiny URL processing
parts:
I filed an issue on this at https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server. Hope that's the right place.

Meanwhile, I've also created a demonstration of how to create a URL-based, multi-page, reactive Shiny web site using the URL "search" protocol. (The issue in this thread needs to be fixed to use the more appropriate URL "path" protocol.

The main advantage is that you don't need the memory to load the entire site into Shiny-Server at startup; only the server code for the current page is ever loaded. It also provides a separate file for each page to help keep things organized.

The code is here: https://github.com/open-meta/uiStub

You can see it running here: https://open-meta.shinyapps.io/uistub/

Tom

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny URL processing
parts: Yeah, that's a totally valid strategy--I've used something similar myself at times. The only thing I would tell you is to absolutely NOT source(fname) UNLESS you have whitelisted the value of fname to be one that you're aware is legitimate (and I do not mean file.exists, but rather, hardcode the filenames that are legitimate). This is to prevent a malicious user from being able to execute literally any .R file they can get onto the server.
